2027-01-14.title: Second Thursday of Denha · St Devasahayam
2027-01-14.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you
Even the wind and the sea obey him
2027-01-14.alt: Season of Denha. St Devasahayam, martyr: Romans 9:30–33; John 10:31–39.
2027-01-14.verse: Resist him, steadfast in your faith, for you know that your brothers and sisters in all the world are undergoing the same kinds of suffering.
theo: At evening, after a long day of teaching, Jesus says to his disciples: “Let us go across to the other side.” On the lake “a great windstorm arose, and the waves beat into the boat”, while Jesus is “in the stern, asleep on the cushion”. The frightened disciples wake him: “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?” He rises, rebukes the wind and says to the sea: “Peace! Be still!” Then comes the question for every age of the Church: “Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?” The disciples are left wondering: “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?” This is a true Denha: the one asleep in their boat is the Lord of creation, the God who “made the storm be still” (Psalm 107:29).

Peter, who was in that boat, later writes to Christians facing persecution: “Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.” The disciples' cry, do you not care, receives its answer: he cares. But Peter is realistic: “Like a roaring lion your adversary the devil prowls around, looking for someone to devour. Resist him, steadfast in your faith.” Today the Church in India honours St Devasahayam, who lived this word. Born Neelakanta Pillai, an official in the service of the kingdom of Travancore, he was baptised in 1745 and took the name Lazarus, Devasahayam. After his Baptism he refused to treat anyone as untouchable; for his faith he was arrested, paraded through towns and kept in chains for nearly three years, and at Aralvaimozhy in 1752 he was shot dead. The storm did not cease for him on earth, but Christ was in his boat, and his faith did not fail. The first reading of his memorial says it: “whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.”
outline: Ask: what storm are you in right now?
Jesus, Lord of wind and sea.
Point 2 · Cast all your anxiety on him
St Devasahayam, faithful in the storm.
“Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?”
live: Write down your heaviest worry today, offer it to Jesus in prayer or at Holy Qurbana, and say: you care for me.
Through the prayers of St Devasahayam, pray for Christians in India and elsewhere who suffer for their faith.
2027-01-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, you slept in the boat and rose to command the wind and the sea. When storms rise in my life, let me cast all my anxiety on you, because you care for me. Through the prayers of St Devasahayam, who stayed steadfast in faith through chains and death, keep me firm and unashamed in confessing you. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is the Lord's presence in the boat of the Church. The Body of Christ that St Devasahayam received is the strength of martyrs and the peace of the anxious.

illus: St Devasahayam was born Neelakanta Pillai near Nagercoil. After his Baptism he took the name Lazarus, Devasahayam in Tamil and Malayalam, meaning “God is my help”. Arrested in 1749, he was paraded through towns and kept in chains for nearly three years, praying and encouraging those who came to him. He was shot dead at Aralvaimozhy in 1752, and was canonised in 2022.

Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you (1 Peter 5:7). What anxiety do I need to hand over?

homily: Dear friends, the disciples are crossing the lake at evening when a great windstorm arises and the waves begin to fill the boat. Jesus is asleep on a cushion. They wake him: Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing? (Mark 4:38).

Jesus rises and says to the sea: Peace! Be still! And there is a dead calm. Then he asks them: why are you afraid? Have you still no faith? (Mark 4:39–40). The disciples ask the question of Denha: who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

Years later Peter, who was in that boat, writes: cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you (1 Peter 5:7). And he warns: the devil prowls around like a roaring lion; resist him, steadfast in your faith (1 Peter 5:8–9).

Today we honour St Devasahayam. After his Baptism he would not deny Christ. For nearly three years he was kept in chains, and at Aralvaimozhy in 1752 he gave his life. The storm did not stop for him, but Christ was in his boat.
Let us hand our worries to the Lord who cares for us, and ask St Devasahayam to make us steadfast in faith. Amen.
kids: Children, once there was a big storm and the disciples were scared, but Jesus said: Peace! Be still! And the sea became calm. When you are scared, say: Jesus, you are in my boat. I trust you!

sub: The Lord of wind and sea.

as it is written, “See, I am laying in Zion a stone that will make people stumble, a rock that will make them fall, and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.”
